method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies' (published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020)). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC7251883). The published correction (PMC7409715, 5 August 2020) replaces Figure 2 only (gene names in the diagnostic flowchart); no recommendation quoted here is affected. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); the claim on the six disorders, their genes and inheritance is quoted from Table 1's row lines. Table 3 (symptoms and signs) and Table 4 (drugs and doses) were not extracted (merged cells).

claims.claim: **BH4 deficiencies are six rare neurometabolic disorders** of BH4 synthesis or regeneration. They deplete dopamine and serotonin, and cause hyperphenylalaninaemia (HPA) in all types except AD-GTPCHD and SRD.
claims.source_text: Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies comprise a group of six rare neurometabolic disorders caused by pathogenic variants in five genes responsible for the biosynthesis and regeneration of BH4 … a disturbance of BH4 metabolism results in a severe depletion of all monoamine neurotransmitters. … hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA) is present in all BH4 deficiencies apart from autosomal dominant guanosine triphosphate cyclohydrolase I deficiency (AD-GTPCHD) and sepiapterin reductase deficiency (SRD)
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BH4 deficiencies are around 1-2% of HPA found on newborn screening;** PTPS deficiency is the most frequent (about 54%), then DHPR deficiency (about 33%).
claims.source_text: BH4 deficiencies are presumed to constitute around 1-2% of these cases. PTPS deficiency (PTPSD) is the most frequent of all HPA -associated BH4 deficiencies (approx. 54%), followed by DHPR deficiency (DHPRD, approx. 33%)
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider a BH4 deficiency** with unexplained hypotonia or hypertonia, dystonia or oculogyric crises, parkinsonism, autonomic dysfunction, or symptoms that fluctuate through the day.
claims.source_text: R#1: (strong): In patients with unexplained alterations in muscle tone (hypotonia/hypertonia), movement disorders (dystonia, oculogyric crises), parkinsonism or hypokinetic rigid syndrome, autonomic dysfunction or diurnal fluctuation of symptoms, BH4Ds should be considered.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider AD-GTPCHD (dopa-responsive dystonia)** when dystonia, especially of the legs, starts in the first or second decade with diurnal fluctuation and normal development.
claims.source_text: R#4: (strong): In patients with dystonia, especially of the lower limbs, with onset in the first or second decade of life associated with diurnal fluctuation of symptoms and normal development, possibly accompanied by parkinsonism, AD-GTPCHD should be considered.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The six disorders, their genes and inheritance (Table 1):** AD-GTPCHD (Segawa disease or dopa-responsive dystonia, DYT5a; GCH1; autosomal dominant); and, all autosomal recessive, AR-GTPCHD (GCH1), PTPSD (PTS), SRD (SPR), DHPR deficiency (QDPR) and PCDD (primapterinuria; PCBD1).
claims.source_text: [Table 1] Nomenclature of BH 4 disorders [Table 1 row 1] Disease name: Autosomal dominant GTP cyclohydrolase I deficiency · Alternative disease name: Segawa disease Dopa-responsive dystonia · Disease abbreviation: AD-GTPCHD, DYT5a · Gene symbol: GCH1 · Mode of inheritance: AD · Affected enzyme: GTPCH I · Disease OMIM#: 128230 [Table 1 row 2] Disease name: Autosomal recessive GTP cyclohydrolase I deficiency · Alternative disease name: - · Disease abbreviation: AR-GTPCHD, DYT/PARK- GCH1 · Gene symbol: GCH1 · Mode of inheritance: AR · Affected enzyme: GTPCH I · Disease OMIM#: 233910 [Table 1 row 3] Disease name: 6-pyruvoyl-tetrahydropterin synthase deficiency · Alternative disease name: - · Disease abbreviation: PTPSD, DYT/PARK- PTS · Gene symbol: PTS · Mode of inheritance: AR · Affected enzyme: PTPS · Disease OMIM#: 261640 [Table 1 row 4] Disease name: Sepiapterin reductase deficiency · Alternative disease name: - · Disease abbreviation: SRD, DYT/PARK- SPR · Gene symbol: SPR · Mode of inheritance: AR · Affected enzyme: SR · Disease OMIM#: 612716 [Table 1 row 5] Disease name: Q-dihydropteridine reductase deficiency · Alternative disease name: - · Disease abbreviation: DHRPD, DYT/PARK- QDPR · Gene symbol: QDPR · Mode of inheritance: AR · Affected enzyme: DHPR · Disease OMIM#: 261630 [Table 1 row 6] Disease name: Pterin-4-alpha-carbinolamine dehydratase deficiency · Alternative disease name: Primapterinuria · Disease abbreviation: PCDD · Gene symbol: PCBD1 · Mode of inheritance: AR · Affected enzyme: PCD · Disease OMIM#: 264070
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Newborn screening for PKU may give the first clue** (HPA) to AR-GTPCHD, PTPSD, DHPRD or PCDD, but it cannot detect AD-GTPCHD or SRD.
claims.source_text: Detection of HPA may be the first clue for underlying AR-GTPCHD, PTPSD, DHPRD or PCDD. … R#6 (strong): NBS is not a suitable diagnostic tool for AD-GTPCH and SRD.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer HPA found on screening to a specialised metabolic centre** for work-up and prompt treatment.
claims.source_text: R#7 (GPP): Patients diagnosed with HPA on NBS should be referred to a specialized metabolic centre for further diagnostic evaluation and prompt initiation of treatment.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In every screen-detected HPA, analyse pterins (urine or dried blood spot) and measure DHPR enzyme activity in a dried blood spot;** pterins alone cannot rule out DHPR deficiency.
claims.source_text: R#9 (strong): Strong recommendation for the analysis of pterins in urine or DBS in patients with HPA on NBS. Pterin analysis cannot rule out DHPRD … R#11 (strong): Strong recommendation for the analysis of DHPR enzyme activity in DBS in patients with HPA in NBS and/or in case of clinical suspicion of disorders of BH4 deficiency.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CSF HVA, 5-HIAA, pterins and 5-MTHF differentiate the BH4 deficiencies;** confirm any biochemical diagnosis with molecular genetic testing.
claims.source_text: R#12 (strong): CSF analysis of HVA, 5-HIAA, pterins and 5-MTHF is a reliable diagnostic method to differentiate between the BH4Ds. … R#15 (strong): Biochemical diagnosis of BH4Ds should be confirmed by molecular genetic analysis.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not delay treatment:** long-term neurodevelopmental outcome depends strongly on starting effective therapy early.
claims.source_text: The long-term neurodevelopmental outcome of BH4D patients is strongly influenced by the early initiation of effective treatment [], therefore therapy must not be delayed.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Control Phe in the BH4 deficiencies with HPA** (AR-GTPCHD, PTPSD, DHPRD, PCDD), by Phe-reduced diet or sapropterin, with Phe targets as for PKU. **Do not** use a Phe-reduced diet in AD-GTPCHD or SRD, nor as the only treatment for neurological symptoms.
claims.source_text: R#30 (strong): Phe control should be applied in BH4Ds with HPA (AR-GTPCHD, PTPSD, DHPRD and PCDD). Phe control may be achieved by Phe-reduced diet or sapropterin dihydrochloride supplementation (see below). Phe levels should be regularly monitored in DBS or blood. Target ranges should be determined by local recommendations for the dietary treatment of PKU. … R#31 (strong): Phe-reduced diet should not be used in BH4Ds without HPA (AD-GTPCHD and SRD). R#32 (strong): Phe-reduced diet should not be used in monotherapy for the treatment of neurological symptoms in BH4Ds.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Sapropterin is the treatment of choice in AR-GTPCHD, PTPSD and PCDD:** once daily, titrated to Phe levels. In PCDD it can be tried off after the first year of life with careful Phe monitoring.
claims.source_text: Sapropterin dihydrochloride is the treatment of choice in AR-GTPCHD, PTPSD, and PCDD. It should be administered once daily and doses should be titrated according to Phe levels. … In PCDD, discontinuation of sapropterin dihydrochloride supplementation can be attempted after the first year of life under careful Phe level monitoring.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In DHPR deficiency, a Phe-reduced diet is the preferred method;** sapropterin can still be considered, because evidence of harm is scarce.
claims.source_text: R#34 (conditional): In DHPRD, Phe-reduced diet and not the supplementation of sapropterin hydrochloride is nowadays considered the method of choice for the control of HPA. Since the available evidence against the use of sapropterin dihydrochloride is scarce, sapropterin dihydrochloride can be considered in DHPRD patients.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **L-Dopa, always with a decarboxylase inhibitor (4:1), is first-line** in AD-GTPCHD, AR-GTPCHD, DHPRD, PTPSD and SRD.
claims.source_text: R#36 (strong): L-Dopa should always be given in combination with a DC inhibitor (4:1 ratio) and should be the first line of treatment in AD-GTPCHD, AR-GTPCHD, DHPRD, PTPSD, and SRD.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start L-Dopa low, in several daily doses, and titrate slowly;** the target in infants under 40 kg (except AD-GTPCHD) is 10 mg/kg/day if tolerated. AD-GTPCHD usually responds to lower doses.
claims.source_text: R#37 (strong): The L-Dopa/DC inhibitor starting dose should be low, distributed in several daily dosages and slowly titrated depending on the clinical symptoms. … the target treatment dose in all infants (below 40 kg body weight) with BH4D (apart from AD-GTPCHD) is 10 mg/kg BW/d (if clinically tolerated). Some patients require higher doses. In AD-GTPCHD, most patients obtain complete symptom control with lower doses of L-Dopa /DC inhibitor.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP) is recommended in DHPRD, PTPSD and SRD** (conditionally in AR-GTPCHD). Start it after L-Dopa, at a lower dose, and do not change both drugs at once.
claims.source_text: In patients with DHPRD, PTPSD, and SRD, benefits clearly outweigh adverse effects, leading to a strong recommendation for the use of 5-HTP in these disorders. … R#40 (strong): 5-HTP should follow initiation of the L-Dopa/DC inhibitor treatment. There is no clear evidence for a starting dose; however, it should be lower than the L-Dopa dose (e.g. Table 4). It should not be changed at the same time as L-Dopa to clearly distinguish clinical effects.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give folinic acid in DHPR deficiency, not folic acid,** which can worsen cerebral folate deficiency. Consider folinic acid in any BH4 deficiency with low CSF 5-MTHF.
claims.source_text: R#41 (strong): Folinic acid supplementation should be used in patients with DHPRD. Note: Cerebral folate deficiency may even be aggravated by the administration of folic acid! … R#42 (conditional): Folinic acid supplementation should be considered in any patient with BH4D found to have low 5-MTHF concentration in CSF.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second line, for residual symptoms or L-Dopa side effects:** a dopamine agonist, preferably non-ergot (pramipexole, ropinirole, rotigotine) or bromocriptine with cardiac screening; or a MAO inhibitor.
claims.source_text: R#43 (conditional): Dopamine agonists can be considered as second line treatment in all BH4Ds (apart from PCDD) in combination with first line treatment options if residual symptoms persist despite L-Dopa/DC inhibitor treatment or if dose-limiting L-Dopa/DC inhibitor- associated adverse events occur. Non-ergot derived DAs (pramipexole, ropinirole, rotigotine) or ergot-derived DA without 5HT2b agonist action (bromocriptine) are preferred. … R#44 (GPP): Cardiac screening before and during treatment with bromocriptine (ergot derived DA) is indicated because of the potential risk of cardiac fibrosis. … R#45 (conditional): MAO inhibitors can be considered as second line treatment in AR-GTPCHD, AD-GTPCHD, PTPSD, DHPRD, and SRD in combination with first line treatment options
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **5-HTP combined with an SSRI, especially at very high doses, can cause serotonin syndrome.**
claims.source_text: R#51 (GPP): Caution: According to the guideline group members, the combination of 5-HTP and SSRI treatment, specifically in very high doses, can induce serotonin syndrome!
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **See patients at least yearly with a neurologist experienced in movement or neurometabolic disorders;** during titration see infants every 3 months and older children at least every 6 months.
claims.source_text: R#58 (GPP): BH4D patients should be seen at least yearly by a (child) neurologist with experience in movement disorders or neurometabolic disease, ideally in a multidisciplinary setting. Infants and young children who require frequent dose adjustments during the course of initial dose titration and due to weight gain need to be seen more frequently (e.g. infants every 3 months; older children at least every 6 months)!
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen PCDD patients for low magnesium and for HNF1A-like (MODY3) diabetes in puberty;** follow all patients for psychiatric, behavioural and sleep problems.
claims.source_text: R#3: (strong): Patients with PCDD should be screened for hypomagnesaemia and the development of HNF1A-like MODY3 diabetes during puberty. … R#2: (strong): Clinical follow-up should include the assessment of psychiatric or behavioural problems and sleep disorders.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Plan transition to adult specialist care early;** offer genetic counselling to every family, and provide multidisciplinary supervision during and after pregnancy.
claims.source_text: R#60 (GPP): Begin planning early for transition of BH4D patients to adult care in specialized centers. Multidisciplinary care should be continued. … R#62 (strong): All patients or parents of patients with BH4Ds should be offered standard genetic counselling if available in local care settings. … R#63 (strong): Intensive supervision during and after the pregnancy by a multidisciplinary team should be provided.
claims.locator: Opladen T, López-Laso E, Cortès-Saladelafont E, et al., on behalf of the International Working Group on Neurotransmitter related Disorders (iNTD), Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 15:126, 'Consensus guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiencies', published 26 May 2020 (figure 2 corrected 5 August 2020), https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-020-01379-8, retrieved 2026-09-23
